questions.help: ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS     18.1 Tests to detect alcohol and drugs  If the test result is positive or even negative and the person presents obvious symptoms of being under the influence of alcohol, the investigating official will require a second test of exhaled air to test for alcohol. There is a minimum time set of ten minutes between these tests.(Página 45 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS 18 Screening for blood alcohol or drugsDriving under the influence of alcohol or drugs is punishable by increasingly stricter penalties, including prison sentences.(Página 45 del manual 'Learning to drive')ALCOHOL AND OTHER DRUGS    18.2 Test resultsIf the outcome of the test is positive, the offence is deemed as being very serious, the driver is punished by way of a fine, withdrawal of between 4 and 6 points and, as it is considered a crime against traffic safety, it is also punishable by judicial imprisonment, community service work and / or removal of the right to drive for several years.If the results are negative but the driver displayed obvious symptoms of being under the influence of alcohol or drugs, law enforcement officers can relay this to the Courts by way of other evidence and data.(Página 45 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ILLNESS AND MEDICATION  20 Some illnesses that can affect driving20.1 Respiratory allergiesAllergic rhinitis can reduce the psycho-physical fitness to drive by up to 42%, causing alterations such as the loss of efficiency, lack of attention, a lower concentration level and decreased ability of visual coordination. It reduces the ability to judge stopping distance, thus increasing the risk of a collision.The most common symptoms of this illness are very similar to those of a simple cold: Runny nose, watery eyes, blurred vision, bouts of sneezing (sometimes up to 20 in a row), fatigue, headache, and so on.(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ILLNESS AND MEDICATION       19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisionsTo drive a vehicle requires certain conditions relating to the physical and mental aptitude of the driver to be initially satisfied and thereafter maintained. Therefore, you should always ask your doctor about the precautions to be taken before driving, especially if you have a chronic illness.(Página 46 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: ILLNESS AND MEDICATION 19 The consequences of illnesses and drugs in traffic collisionsSooner or later, everybody suffers from an illness that requires medication to treat it. questions.help: ILLNESS AND MEDICATION     20 Some illnesses that can affect driving 20.3 DepressionIt is the most common form of mental suffering. The driver focuses all his attention on his thoughts and neglects the surroundings.Making valuable information become lost or irrelevant. The driver fails to detect significant information needed for safety and requiring driver reaction, especially in more complex situations.Increasing insecurity. Depression interferes in the decision-making process, so the driver can make mistakes or act unpredictably.Increasing the propensity for sleepiness and fatigue. questions.help: OTHER FACTORS        25 Clothing  25.1 The clothing of motorcyclistA motorcycle does not provide the rider with a secure and protective shell. This makes the rider vulnerable in road traffic collisions; to the elements, such as, in the cold, wind, rain, and so on. The body of the rider and any passenger realises the force of all of these external elements, the weather and any possible impact. It is therefore absolutely essential to use a dress code that adequately protects them all of the time regardless of the time of year.The motorcyclist’s outfit has to be colourful and eye-catching, and should be made of leather or other similar material. It should have contrasting colours and design, with reflective bands that allow it to be distinguished from a distance.A ‘set of leathers’ (a leather jacket and trousers) is advocated, as it will:Does not flap with the air.Protects against the wind during the trip.Provide protection from possible damage, scrapes and consequent rubbing or contact sores to the rider. In the event of falling off abrasive wounds are minimised.(Página 50 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help: OTHER FACTORS      25 Clothing 25.1 The clothing of motorcyclistWhen riding a motorcycle it is recommendable to wear gloves. If the rider falls or slips off typically the hands receive the force and impact as the rider automatically responds with the hands. Inevitably grazes and wounds, subject to the risk also of serious infection, will occur to the hands without gloves. The most suitable type are leather gloves that should not be too restrictive and allow for a firm grip to be maintained. They should be lined and have protective areas, with ventilation whilst also being light in weight.Strong, protective boots are another must for the rider. These protect the feet and ankles (it is advisable that they are higher in length, to also protect the legs). Ideally they should be leather, with small heels, so as to hold well in the stirrups or rests.Always avoid using sandals, sports shoes or other unsuitable footwear that offer only minimal protection.(Página 50 del manual 'Learning to drive')
